text:
Marta: quick follow-up from the rollout RFC — thinking about a very small 'micro-bridge' escape hatch between canary and prod to avoid full rollback for short blips. want quick sanity check before i write a formal RFC.

Arjun: curious — who makes the open/close decision? observer service or router hot-path? big design split.

Marta: leaning hybrid: router keeps ultra-fast heuristics (local latency/5xx thresholds) for immediate short-circuit, observer can issue timebound bridge tokens for rollout-level decisions. router also exposes light health hints.

Alex: hybrid is reasonable. concerns: cache-warmth loss when sessions move -> latency spike. do we accept cold paths or attempt prefetch?

Jin: token should carry a cache-hint (hashed) so downstream can best-effort prefetch without leaking internals. token must be signed and non-PII.

Marta: proposed token schema (opaque to router): `microbridge_v1:{cohort,session,cache_hint_hash,issuer,exp}`. router forwards if present.

SRE-Oncall: how do we prevent prod overload if bridge sends lots of traffic at once? need throttles and budget windows.

Marta: bridge config sketch in the runtime:```
micro_bridge:
  enabled: true
  ttl_ms: 2500
  max_inflight_per_cohort: 40
  global_hedge_fraction: 0.05
  surge_backoff_ms: 300
```

Arjun: add hysteresis: don't open bridge unless observer confidence < 0.7 for 3 consecutive windows. router fast-heuristic can open for brief spikes but observer overrides persistent changes.

Alex: also need per-tenant override — premium tenants might want immediate failover to their dedicated fallback, others go through bridge.

Jin: security note: sign tokens with rollout-controller key, verify in router. cache_hint must be a one-way hash. audit logs for token issuance.

Marta: operational signals to surface: `microbridge.open_rate`, `microbridge.queue_ms.p95`, `microbridge.fallback_to_prod_rate`, `microbridge.rejected_overflow_count`. trigger alert when prod_overflow_events > X or queue_ms.p95 > Y.

SRE-Oncall: runbook idea: 1) observer opens bridge (timebound) 2) router honors token + enforces per-cohort budget 3) if prod overloaded, bridge rejects and observer escalates/rolls back 4) human can force-close token via rollout controller. include safe defaults.

Arjun: for router heuristics strawman i'll draft: keep decision latency <50ms, use EWMA latency + short 5xx window, respect per-tenant quotas. will microbenchmark.

Alex: i'll draft dashboard and ops knobs (urgent alert thresholds, knob to flip to direct rollback, per-tenant bypass switch).

Jin: i'll write token spec + signing verification steps and short security checklist (no PII, rotate keys, audit).

Marta: API contracts to include in RFC: `rollout-controller -> observer: open_microbridge(cohort, reason, timeout_ms)`; `observer -> router: publish_microbridge_token(token)`; router emits `microbridge.state` metrics. all calls idempotent.

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/microbridge-proto -> staging (id: d-2026-03-23-09). logs: https://ci.redwood/d-2026-03-23-09 :rocket:

Marta: perfect. i'll put together the RFC draft with diagrams and the minimal API + config defaults. aiming to post by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
